HIGH COURT OF CHHATTISGARH, BILASPUR  MCRC No. 5365 of 2023   Filip Tigga S/o Shri Kalpnath Tigga Aged About 24 Years R/o Katkalo  Koronjpara, P.S. Sitapur, District : Surguja (Ambikapur), Chhattisgarh
Versus   State Of Chhattisgarh
Through P.S. Incharge P.S. Sitapur, District : Surguja  (Ambikapur), Chhattisgarh

For Applicant : Shri Dhaneshwar Yadav, Advocate For Respondent/State : Shri Suyash Dhar, PL ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Hon'ble Smt Justice Rajani Dubey Order on Board 18.08.2023 1.

Applicant has preferred this 3rd bail application under Section 439 of the CrPC for grant of regular bail as he is arrested in connection with Crime No.134 of 2022, registered at Police Station- Sitapur, district- Surguja (CG) for the offence punishable under Sections 376(2)(n), 596, and 509 of the IPC, 67(a) of the IT Act, and 3/4/6 of the Indecent Representation of Women (Prohibition) Act.

2. First bail application has been dismissed as withdrawn with liberty to revive the same after examination of the prosecutrix on 17.10.2022 in MCRC- 7315 of 2022 and Second bail application is dismissed as withdrawn in MCRC-3660 of 2023.
3.

Case of the prosecution in brief, is that prosecutrix/complainant lodged a written complaint on 07.05.2022 against the applicant herein alleging that applicant made physical relationship with the prosecutrix by threatening her and also took her indecent photographs and made it viral.
On the basis of written complaint, FIR has been registered against the applicant.
Learned counsel for the applicant submits that applicant is innocent and has been falsely implicated in the case.
He further submits that prosecutrix has not supported the case of prosecution.
She made the complaint in fit of anger.
Applicant is in jail since 07.05.2022.
Charge-sheet has been filed and there is no likelihood of his case being decided in near future

,
therefore, he may be released on bail.

sentences.text: On the other hand, learned counsel for the State opposes the bail application.
6. Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the rejection order of the Court below.

7. Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, and further considering the fact that prosecutrix/complainant herself not supported the prosecution case and turned hostile, looking to the detention period of the applicant, and the trial may take some time, without further commenting on merits of the case, I am inclined to release the applicant on bail.
8. Accordingly, bail application is allowed.

9. It is directed that applicant shall be released on bail on his executing a personal bond for a sum of Rs.25,000/- (Rupees twenty-five thousand only) with one surety of the like sum to the satisfaction of the trial Court for his appearance before the said Court as and when directed.
Certified copy as per rules.

Sd/-
